This is the hand-tuned exploration floor for policy reuse that the yield rule is meant to replace.

closest_prior.citation: Yardimci & Cogurcu, 'Uncertainty-Gated Exploration Noise Suppresses Task Collapse in Online RL Fine-Tuning of a Flow-Matching VLA Policy', arXiv 2609.28838, Sep 2026
closest_prior.overlap: Adaptive per-stream exploration noise in multi-task PPO fine-tuning (LIBERO-10), set by an RND novelty score times critic-based competence. It compares fixed noise with ReinFlow-style learned noise and prevents task collapse. It argues explicitly against noise driven by success rate, so expect a reviewer to cite it.

closest_prior.citation: Plappert et al., 'Parameter Space Noise for Exploration', ICLR 2018, arXiv 1706.01905
closest_prior.overlap: Adapts the noise scale online by a multiplicative up/down rule so that the perturbation stays at a target distance delta in action space. This is closed-loop noise control with a distance target, not an outcome target.

closest_prior.citation: An et al., POLARIS recipe (HKU/ByteDance Seed blog, 2025); see also AceReason-Nemotron 1.1, arXiv 2506.13284
closest_prior.overlap: Runs a temperature sweep before RL to set the starting exploration dose from no-training rollouts (start inside the 'controlled exploration zone'), then raises the temperature at each stage to keep diversity at its earlier level. AceReason sets the temperature so that temperature-adjusted entropy stays near 0.3. Both calibrate the dose in closed form and then retarget it, using diversity or entropy instead of a success budget.

closest_prior.citation: Montenegro, Mussi, Metelli, Papini, 'Learning Optimal Deterministic Policies with Stochastic Policy Gradients', ICML 2024 (PMLR 235)
closest_prior.overlap: Theory for choosing the exploration level when a stochastic policy is trained but its deterministic version is deployed: sample complexity trades off against deterministic performance. This is the deterministic-lag trade-off that self-retirement is supposed to handle, and reviewers will use it as the yardstick.

closest_prior.citation: Schaul et al., 'Adapting Behaviour for Learning Progress', arXiv 1912.06910, 2019
closest_prior.overlap: A non-stationary bandit adjusts policy stochasticity online from a learning-progress proxy and matches per-task tuning on Atari at a fraction of the cost. This is the 'one online rule replaces per-task exploration tuning' claim, made for discrete control.

closest_prior.citation: Zhang et al., 'RobustVLA: Robustness-Aware Reinforcement Post-Training for VLA Models', arXiv 2511.01331, 2025
closest_prior.overlap: Raises or lowers the injected action and observation noise level by thresholds on a smoothed success rate during PPO post-training. This is a success-thresholded noise controller, but it serves robustness and points the other way: more noise as competence rises.

closest_prior.citation: OpenAI, 'Solving Rubik's Cube with a Robot Hand' (Automatic Domain Randomization), arXiv 1910.07113, 2019
closest_prior.overlap: A controller driven by performance thresholds widens or narrows distribution parameters online. The same outcome-threshold controller, applied to environment randomization instead of action noise.

closest_prior.citation: Raffin, Kober, Stulp, 'Smooth Exploration for Robotic Reinforcement Learning' (gSDE), CoRL 2021, arXiv 2005.05719
closest_prior.overlap: Temporally correlated, state-dependent exploration noise for robots. The proposed a2r comparison of i.i.d. and correlated gripper noise at equal sigma is prior art, not a contribution.

result.risks:
1) Novelty is thin. I found no paper that sets a reused robot policy's action-std floor from a success-yield target, but every piece already exists. Exploration intensity gated by success rate, with a closed-loop global coefficient, is in AER (2025). Feedback control toward a pass-rate target is in Prefix Sampling (2026). Per-task exploration so that mastered tasks stop exploring is in PCGrad/MT-SAC. Learned bounded noise that decays as success saturates is in ReinFlow. Floors picked by sweep are in DPPO. Dose probing before RL is in POLARIS. The projection point is correct. It is confirmed in a2r policy.py:144 (forward torch.maximum), :414 (post-step clamp to [-3, 0]) and :438 (only the effective std is logged), and in pve wrwl/ppo.py:237/244 (forward clamp). But it is folklore-level: there is no paper on it, and reviewers will call it an implementation note.

2) Today's own data weakens the retrospective validation. On Stack, the 0.6 floor (yield ~1%, 7-17 successes per 1024-episode iteration) reached 90% at 3.58/2.56M steps, the same as the 1.0 floor (~11%) at 2.56/3.58M. On PushRetreat-10, 0.6 (0.61-0.82M) tied 1.0 (0.61-1.23M). So any q* between ~1% and ~15% 'reproduces the hand-picked doses'; the q* = 10% fit is not evidence. On ManiSkill the dose response above ignition looks flat. The only costly mistakes are no floor when the source fails and a floor when it already succeeds, so the rule may reduce to a binary gate on the frozen source's yield, which is a one-line heuristic. The U-shaped response that would give the rule value is in a2r, not ManiSkill. On egg-p75, success at iterations 30-60 was 0.03 / 0.56-0.63 / 0.00-0.03 for floors 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0, and 0.98 vs 0.47 at iteration 140 for 0.6 vs 1.0.

3) The online part may do nothing, or may even hurt.
(a) With projection, lowering phi does not lower sigma; only PPO can. Today, unclamped stds rose while successes still depended on noise (0.6 to 1.4 in the anchored runs; 0.27 to 0.45-0.66 outside the seam), so E can collapse to D, and the deterministic lag remains.
(b) A larger learned sigma widens PPO's effective trust region for the mean. That is a suspected cause of the PushRetreat-6 deterministic collapse (eval fell from 0.67-0.82 to 0-0.02), so freeing sigma can make the lag worse.
(c) The controller reads training success under noise. That signal has survivor bias in the first iterations (PushRetreat), and it is not deterministic success, so the floor can retire while the mean policy is still poor and then re-ignite: oscillation.
(d) A two-sided target that holds training success near 10% starves the middle phase, which ran faster with more yield (train success reached 50% at 0.61-0.77M with 1.0 vs 0.92-1.02M with 0.6). The rule must be one-sided: raise the floor while success < q*, decay it only after sustained success >> q*.

4) Risks specific to a2r.
- Since log_std is clamped to at most 0, sigma <= 1. At a 1.0 floor, projection and clamp are identical.
- Per-task floors change each task's KL scale (KL is proportional to dmu^2/sigma^2), and the LR controller averages per-task KL. Zero-success tasks with high floors pull the mean KL down, the LR rises, and mastered tasks with low sigma take larger steps. That is the same coupling behind the 97.9% to 32-36% joint collapse, so per-task KL normalisation is needed, or boosted tasks must be excluded from the KL mean.
- Upstream starts (hang pregrasp at 0/137) may have zero yield at every sigma <= 1. The controller then saturates at phi_max and injects maximum noise with no signal into the shared trunk. Cap it and freeze when the yield stays 0.
- Check that rollout_std (policy.py:223) is unset in the configs used.
- The retrospective egg/hang yield check needs the lab's exact starting checkpoints (the debug-egg-p75 ablation).

5) Statistics. With 3 seeds the 'C halves B's ignition-time spread' criterion is meaningless: a variance ratio estimated from n = 3 per arm has a 95% interval spanning roughly 40x. The first crossing of 0.9 with 128-256 eval episodes jitters by about one interval.

6) Hyperparameter creep. q*, gamma, eps, phi_min, phi_max and the RMS window only count as 'no per-task tuning' if shared values work everywhere. Insensitivity to q* has to be shown.

result.verdict:
This idea is incremental, cheap and probably small. As a whole it is not done already: I found no paper that sets a reused robot policy's action-noise floor from a success-yield budget. But the logic is published elsewhere: success-gated exploration intensity with closed-loop control (AER, 2025), pass-rate feedback control (Prefix Sampling, 2026), per-task temperatures for multi-task RL (PCGrad/MT-SAC), learned bounded noise that decays as success saturates (ReinFlow), floor sweeps (DPPO) and dose probing before RL (POLARIS).

The projection finding is real; I confirmed it in a2r policy.py:144/414/438 and pve ppo.py:237/244. It is still a footnote, not a paper result.

The bigger problem is that today's own logs undercut the headline. Stack at a 0.6 floor (~1% yield) reached 90% as fast as at 1.0 (~11%), and on PushRetreat-10 the two floors also tied. So 'q* = 10% reproduces our hand-picked doses' fits any q* from ~1% to ~15%. On ManiSkill the rule will likely reduce to a binary gate on the frozen source's yield, and with projection the online retirement may do nothing, because PPO itself keeps sigma high while successes depend on noise.

The one place a dose rule could really pay off is a2r, where the egg dose response is U-shaped (0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 give 0.03 / 0.98 / 0.47) and the 50-task plan cannot be hand-tuned.

Recommendation: spend under 2 GPU-h on Gate 0 and Gate 1 (raw log_std read and pre-registered yield predictions, including egg and hang) before any RL grid. Continue only if a single q* picks egg 0.6, hang 0.3 and PushRetreat-6 none. Even then, present it as the 'ignite' component of a reuse recipe, paired with a consolidation step, not as the RSS headline. A headline-worthy result would be a2r's joint run where one budget replaces the hand-set per-task floors without regressing mastered tasks through the KL-adaptive LR coupling.

Incremental, and largely falsified by today's logs before any new run.
- The data recipe is published. Takeover plus success-filtered distillation is PLD (ICLR 2026) and TILDE (Oct 2026); success-filtered BC from RL teachers is RLDG and OmniReset.
- The theory is published too. The 'EM step by Tweedie' is RWR, PoWER and ReST-EM, and 'the student consolidates' is SFT-sharpening. The only new element is stopping the teacher early.
- The claimed >= 30% saving needs a window that does not exist on Stack: there the deterministic policy reaches 0.9 (1.33M / 1.43M full fine-tune; 2.66-3.17M frozen) before or with the noisy one.
- PlaceCube does have the window. But the teacher hovers at the target, so success-conditioned labels barely move the mean: the bound is sigma*sqrt((1-V)/V), and a calibrated toy gives a gripper label of -0.85 vs -1.0, so the student never releases.

Do not build takeover, MeanFlow or the a2r port. Spend at most about one day plus one night on the L0-L4 + drop-floor test. The most likely result is L3 ≈ L0, with A > 0 filtering or dropping the floor closing the gap. That would be a consolidation-schedule detail for the WRWL recipe (ignite with the floor, then drop it or self-distil on advantage-filtered actions), not a separate RSS paper.
